## Project Overview

This project investigates consumer brand choice behavior using **Multinomial Logit** and **Latent Class Analysis (LCA)**. The analysis focuses on identifying distinct consumer segments to optimize pricing strategies and understand market heterogeneity.

## Methodology
This analysis moves beyond aggregate preferences by employing **Latent Class Analysis (LCA)** to uncover hidden segments within the consumer population.

### 1. Baseline Modeling (Multinomial Logit)
Initially, a standard Multinomial Logit (MNL) model was fitted to establish baseline average effects.

Result: Price has a significant negative effect (-0.37), and feature ads have a positive effect (+0.49) on brand choice across the aggregate population.

### 2. Identifying Heterogeneity (LCA)

To capture market heterogeneity, I fitted Finite Mixture Models using the flexmix package, testing from k=1 to k=6 classes.

Model Selection: Based on the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) and model interpretability, a 4-class model was selected.
